newsitem.title: USA: Phillips says LLDPE catalyst trials succeed.
newsitem.headline: Phillips says LLDPE catalyst trials succeed.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said Thursday trials using its own metallocene catalyst technology to produce linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) on commercial scale has been successful.
It said its metallocene catalysts are new "precision" catalysts that give extended manufacturing control over the molecular structure and properties of polyethylene.
When used to manufacture LLDPE, the result is a film "of exceptional clarity and strength" that is ideal for food packaging, it said.
Phillips said the catalysts were tested at its chemical complex in Houston.
It said that because the catalysts were designed for the company's slurry loop process in making polyethylene, it expects licensing revenues to increase.
The slurry loop technology is licensed in 14 countries and accounts for 30 percent of the world's high density polyethylene production, it said.
Jack Howe, a senior vice president in charge of natural gas liquids, chemicals and plastics, said that the new catalysts would boost Phillips' position as a major global supplier of polyethylene.
Phillips will also be able to enter the LLDPE market by using exising plants and technology, he added.
